title: Build perfect cubes with linking cubes and write them with exponents (4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64)

lesson.title: Cubes and the Little 3 Up High

steps.say: You already know how to build a perfect square with tiles, like four rows of four tiles making sixteen. Today we take that same idea off the table and into the air, and give it a name: a perfect cube.

Imagine you snap linking cubes together to make a solid block that is four cubes long, four cubes wide, and four cubes tall. Every edge is the same, so the block is a perfect cube. You already know how to find the volume of a rectangular prism, so count the little cubes the same way: four times four times four.

visual.caption: A 4 by 4 by 4 block of linking cubes

steps.say: Writing four times four times four every single time gets tiring, so we use a shortcut. We write four with a tiny three up high, and we read it as four cubed, or four to the power of three. The big four is the base, the number we keep multiplying. The little three is the exponent, and it tells us how many fours to multiply together. So four cubed equals sixty four.

visual.caption: 4 cubed = 64 small cubes fill this block

steps.say: Here is the trap almost everybody falls into. Some people look at four cubed and say twelve, because they multiply four by three. But the little three is not a factor you multiply by. It is a counter telling you how many fours to use. Three fours multiplied is sixty four, not twelve. Same warning for squares: three squared is three times three, which is nine, not six.

visual.caption: The right answer is much bigger than the mistake

steps.say: Let us do one more with real life. Say you are packing sugar cube sized ice cubes into a small cooler box that is three cubes long, three cubes wide and three cubes tall. Three cubed means three times three times three. Three times three is nine, and nine times three is twenty seven. So twenty seven ice cubes fill it, and twenty seven is a perfect cube.
So remember: the little three up high never means multiply by three. It means build a solid block with three equal edges, and count every cube inside.

lesson.answer: Four cubed means four times four times four, which is 64 — the exponent counts the factors, it never means times three.

practice.question: You are stacking sugar cubes into a perfect cube shaped box for a school bake sale in Vancouver. Each edge of the stack is five sugar cubes long, five wide, and five tall. Draw a quick sketch of the block if it helps. Write this using an exponent, then find how many sugar cubes you need in total.
practice.answer: 5 cubed, written as 5 with a small 3 up high, equals 5 times 5 times 5. Five times five is 25, and 25 times 5 is 125. So you need 125 sugar cubes. (Careful: it is not 5 times 3, which would be only 15.)
